Browser.setDownloadBehavior is sent with no browser_context_id, so it always targets the default context. zendriver tracks the result per Tab (_download_behavior). DownloadExpectation enables download events, but set_download_path sends events_enabled unset (false) on the same session. Results: (1) ex.value never resolves when download_file or set_download_path runs inside expect_download; (2) context tabs ignore set_download_path and expect_download times out; (3) one tab's download_file or expect_download silently redirects another tab's downloads. I found no keepalive or timeout that ends the ex.value wait. DownloadExpectation's future has no timeout.

member_verdicts.note: Real Chromium: create_context tab, then set_download_path(d), then clicking a download link saves nothing in d (nor in ~/Downloads). ctx expect_download times out after 5s with no DownloadWillBegin. The control with browser_context_id=ctx.target.browser_context_id saves the file. Side effect: a later download in the default-context main tab (which never set a path) landed in the ctx tab's directory.

Real Chromium, fresh tab: inside expect_download(), download_file(url, name) leaves ex.value unresolved (5s wait_for timeout), and the file is still written to ./downloads despite the 'deny'. Calling set_download_path inside the block behaves the same: no event, file saved. Control: expect_download plus a click after the path is set delivers DownloadWillBegin. Without a user-supplied timeout, await ex.value hangs indefinitely.

Real Chromium: tab_a.set_download_path(dirA), and a link download goes to dirA. Then tab_b.download_file(...) (with a 'no download path set' warning). A later tab_a link download went to ./downloads; dirA kept only the first file.

Real Chromium: tab_b.set_download_path(dirB), and download_file goes to dirB. Then async with tab_a.expect_download(): pass. tab_b._download_behavior still reads 'allow', but the next tab_b.download_file landed in ~/Downloads, not dirB. I removed my stray file ~/Downloads/beref_a106_second.txt afterwards.

Same mechanism and same run as A10.6: DownloadExpectation.__init__ captures tab_a's own (empty) _download_behavior, and __aexit__ restores behavior='default' for the whole default context. groups.summary: I tried to refute all four keys.py members and could not. Each one reproduces in real headless Chromium 141 on Python 3.13. The most serious is A10.5: send_keys(str) sends each emoji grapheme as one 'char' event, and Chrome rejects any text of 4 or more UTF-16 units. So skin-toned emoji, flags and ZWJ sequences raise ProtocolException partway through typing. The other three are wrong-result bugs with lower realism. They only appear on the DOWN_AND_UP path (from_mixed_input, SpecialKeys, or a KeyEvents object the user builds and reuses).

member_verdicts.note: In real Chromium I called send_keys('x'+s+'y') for each case. Thumbs-up (2 UTF-16 units) and e+combining acute (2 units) both work. Thumbs-up with a skin tone (4), the DE flag (4), the family ZWJ emoji (11) and a+3 combining marks (4) each raise ProtocolException "Invalid 'text' parameter", and the field is left holding 'x'. Nothing upstream splits graphemes: KeyEvents.from_text passes the whole grapheme to to_cdp_events(CHAR). The repo test test_visible_events types a thumbs-up emoji, so emoji support is intended.

In KeyEvents.to_down_up_sequence, step 3 releases the modifiers in press order, although its comment says reverse order. It does this before step 4 (main keyup), which then carries modifiers=0. Chrome log for Ctrl+Enter: keyup Control (ctrl=false), then keyup Enter (ctrl=false). For 'A': keyup Shift, then keyup 'a' (shift=false). For Ctrl+Shift+a, Control is released before Shift. Keydown carries the correct modifiers, so shortcuts handled on keydown still work (Ctrl+A/C/V in the repo test).

Offline, KeyEvents('A').to_cdp_events(DOWN_AND_UP) gives Shift plus text 'A' the first time and plain 'a' with no Shift the second time. For '!' the second call gives '1'. In real Chromium, sending the same KeyEvents('A') object twice types 'Aa'. Cause: to_cdp_events assigns self.key = _normalise_key(...). zendriver itself never reuses an instance (from_text and send_keys build new ones), so only user code that reuses the public class is affected.

In real Chromium, send_keys(SpecialKeys.SPACE) and from_mixed_input([' ']) produce keydown key=' ' with code '' (empty) and keyCode 32. TAB gives code 'Tab'. A space is still inserted, and e.key and e.keyCode are correct, so only handlers that check e.code === 'Space' miss it. send_keys(' ') with a str goes through CHAR and sends no keydown at all.

groups.evidence: Probes: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/verify/BE-refute/keys_offline.py and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/verify/BE-refute/keys_real.py. These ran against the repo copy (zendriver.__file__ = /home/user/zendriver/zendriver/__init__.py), headless Chromium 141, Python 3.13.16, with a document-level keydown/keypress/keyup logger. Key output: "A10.5 '<thumbs-up+skin tone>' utf16 4 -> EXC ProtocolException: Invalid 'text' parameter ... value= 'x'"; "A10.9 Ctrl+Enter [...keyup:Control:ctrl=false, keyup:Enter:ctrl=false]"; "A10.11 SPACE ['keydown:\" \"::32', ...]" (empty code); "A10.10 reuse value= 'Aa'". git log -S shows the code arrived in bulk in 5c1a005 and d4d8117. Nothing in history marks the behaviour as deliberate, and no test asserts it.
groups.refinements: A10.5: this is a Chrome limit (text must be under 4 UTF-16 units). Single-codepoint emoji and short combining sequences work; it fails on skin-tone modifiers, flags, keycaps, ZWJ families and long combining clusters. Earlier graphemes have already been typed when it raises. A10.9/A10.11: only the DOWN_AND_UP path is affected (from_mixed_input, SpecialKeys, explicit KeyEvents). Plain send_keys(str) uses CHAR, sends no keydown/keyup, and so cannot show these two bugs. A10.9 matters only to keyup handlers that read modifiers or e.key. Real keyboards also produce Shift-up before A-up during rollover, so robust pages already cope. A10.10 needs explicit reuse of a KeyEvents object.

groups.summary: All seven distinct claims (nine member ids, two of them duplicates) reproduce in real headless Chromium. They are independent local defects in tab.py. None is guarded upstream, none is marked deliberate in git history, and no test asserts the current behaviour. Realism varies: get_all_urls and set_user_agent(accept_language=...) are ordinary uses. The webp crash, ReturnAsStream and quoted filenames need inputs outside the documented happy path. The save_snapshot corruption is Windows-only.

member_verdicts.note: Real Chromium on /docs/index.html: get_all_urls() returned [/sub/page.html, /up.html, /root.html, /images/a.png]. The browser's own resolution is [/docs/style.css, /docs/sub/page.html, /docs/other.html, /up.html, /root.html, https://example.org/page#frag, /docs/images/a.png, /docs/data.txt]. So the relative URLs are resolved against the origin, and bare names (style.css, other.html, data.txt) and '#' URLs are dropped. Cause in Tab.get_all_urls: '/'.join(self.url.rsplit('/')[:3]) plus the 'http'/'//'/'/' and '#' filters.
Duplicate of A7.5. The same real-browser run shows it.

Real headless Chromium after set_user_agent(accept_language='de-DE') and a navigation: navigator.userAgentData.brands goes from [Chromium 141, Not?A_Brand 8] to [], platform goes from 'Linux' to ''. The Sec-CH-UA, Sec-CH-UA-Mobile and Sec-CH-UA-Platform request headers disappear, leaving only Accept-Language: de-DE. Connection._prepare_headless's own docstring says an override without metadata drops client hints. test_set_user_agent_defaults_existing_user_agent checks only the UA and the language.

Real Chromium: download_file(url, 'plain.txt') saved the file. download_file(url, "O'Reilly.txt") returned normally and saved nothing. Runtime.callFunctionOn with that quoting returns ExceptionDetails 'SyntaxError: missing ) after argument list', and Tab.download_file ignores it. JS injection through a crafted url follows from the same %s formatting (assumed, not exploited).

Verified: Page.captureSnapshot output has 71 CRLF, 0 bare LF and is pure ASCII. Python text mode with newline='\r\n' (what open(...,'w') does on Windows) writes b'\r\r\n'. A file rewritten that way renders in Chromium with body innerText '' (empty), while the original renders the page text. Windows itself was not run; that step relies on documented Python behaviour.

Real Chromium: tab.save_screenshot(format='webp') raises UnboundLocalError "cannot access local variable 'ext'". The docstring documents only jpeg and png, so webp is outside the documented contract, but any unknown format crashes the same way instead of failing with a clear error.
Duplicate of A7.9. The same real-browser run shows it.

Real Chromium: 8 back-to-back save_screenshot() calls took 2.13s and returned only 3 unique paths. 3 files were on disk, so 5 screenshots were silently overwritten. A single pair of calls collides only when both fall in the same wall-clock second (a run of 2 did not collide).

Real Chromium: print_to_pdf(path, transfer_mode='ReturnAsStream') writes a 0-byte file and reports success. The control (no kwargs) writes 21313 bytes. The raw CDP call returns data='' and stream handle '1', and IO.read on it yields '%PDF-1' (base64 JVBERi0x), so the handle is live and never closed by zendriver.

Key lines: 'A7.6 after : [[],"",...,"de-DE"]'; 'A7.6 headers after : {Accept-Language: de-DE}'; 'A7.9 webp EXC UnboundLocalError'; 'A7.10 8 calls in 2.13s, returned unique=3, files on disk=3'; 'A7.12 stream size 0' and 'control size 21313'; 'A7.8 win.mhtml -> empty string'; 'A7.7 files: [plain.txt]' and 'ExceptionDetails SyntaxError'. git log -S traces every affected snippet to the bulk import 5c1a005, with no stated intent.
groups.refinements: A7.5/A12.7: correct only for pages served at a directory root, or links written as absolute or root-relative paths. Any page in a subdirectory or with bare relative links gives wrong or missing URLs. The '#' filter also drops absolute links that have fragments. A7.6: affects set_user_agent calls without metadata, both headless and (assumed) headful. When a user passes a custom UA string, there is arguably no correct metadata to send, but the accept_language-only call is a clear regression of the 984bf02 client-hint fix. A7.7: needs a ' or \ in the url or filename. A7.8: Windows only. A7.9: needs a format outside the documented jpeg/png. A7.10: needs two auto-named shots in the same wall-clock second, which is common in loops. A7.12: needs an explicit transfer_mode='ReturnAsStream' kwarg.

groups.summary: Both set_window_state members reproduce in real Chromium: headless, and headful under Xvfb with no window manager. A6.6: when the window is not normal, Chrome only restores it and ignores left/top/width/height, so set_window_size after maximize/minimize/fullscreen silently does nothing to the geometry. A6.7: before switching to a non-normal state, Tab.set_window_state calls itself with the defaults 0,0,1280,720, so the restore geometry is overwritten (and in headful mode the window visibly jumps). The two combine: after tab.maximize(), set_window_size(...) ends up at 0,0 1280x720.

member_verdicts.note: Headless: set_window_size(50,60,800,600), then the state change, then set_window_size(200,100,900,700) ends at state=normal 0,0 1280x720 after maximize, after minimize and after fullscreen. Headful under Xvfb the same happens after fullscreen. A control with raw CDP (Bounds left/top/width/height with no state, sent while maximized) also restored the window to its previous normal geometry, not 200,100 900x700. So Chrome itself drops the geometry on restore, and Tab.set_window_state does not handle it.

Headless: set_window_size(100,50,800,600), then tab.maximize(), then a plain Bounds(window_state=NORMAL) restore gives 0,0 1280x720. The same sequence with a raw CDP maximize restores to 100,50 800x600. Headful under Xvfb (no WM, so maximize itself is a no-op): right after tab.maximize() the window is at 0,0 1280x720 although it was at 100,50 800x600. Cause: await self.set_window_state(state='normal') uses the default left=0, top=0, width=1280, height=720.

groups.evidence: Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/verify/BE-refute/win.py, run headless and under xvfb-run (1920x1080, no window manager), on Python 3.13.16 with Chromium 141. Headless lines: 'set_window_size(200,100,900,700) after maximize: state=normal l=0 t=0 w=1280 h=720'; 'tab.maximize() ... plain restore: state=normal l=0 t=0 w=1280 h=720' versus 'raw maximize ... plain restore: state=normal l=100 t=50 w=800 h=600'; 'raw bounds w/o state while maximized: state=normal l=100 t=50 w=800 h=600'. The code comes from the bulk import 5c1a005. Its comment covers only the normal-to-non-normal direction, and no test exercises it.
groups.refinements: The 0,0 1280x720 result seen in A6.6 actually comes from A6.7's reset. The core of A6.6 (requested bounds dropped while the window is non-normal) holds on its own, as the raw-CDP control shows. Through zendriver's own API, A6.7 is visible only as the headful jump/resize before minimize, maximize or fullscreen, or when the window is restored by raw CDP or by the user, because medimize() always sends 0,0,1280,720 anyway. Headful maximize/minimize could not be checked because Xvfb has no window manager; fullscreen was checked headful. It needs a sequence where the size is set after a state change, which is unusual for most scripts.

groups.summary: Both set_window_state members reproduce in real Chromium: headless, and headful under Xvfb with no window manager. A6.6: when the window is not normal, Chrome only restores it and ignores left/top/width/height, so set_window_size after maximize/minimize/fullscreen silently does nothing to the geometry. A6.7: before switching to a non-normal state, Tab.set_window_state calls itself with the defaults 0,0,1280,720, so the restore geometry is overwritten (and in headful mode the window visibly jumps). The two combine: after tab.maximize(), set_window_size(...) ends up at 0,0 1280x720.

member_verdicts.note: Headless: set_window_size(50,60,800,600), then the state change, then set_window_size(200,100,900,700) ends at state=normal 0,0 1280x720 after maximize, after minimize and after fullscreen. Headful under Xvfb the same happens after fullscreen. A control with raw CDP (Bounds left/top/width/height with no state, sent while maximized) also restored the window to its previous normal geometry, not 200,100 900x700. So Chrome itself drops the geometry on restore, and Tab.set_window_state does not handle it.

Headless: set_window_size(100,50,800,600), then tab.maximize(), then a plain Bounds(window_state=NORMAL) restore gives 0,0 1280x720. The same sequence with a raw CDP maximize restores to 100,50 800x600. Headful under Xvfb (no WM, so maximize itself is a no-op): right after tab.maximize() the window is at 0,0 1280x720 although it was at 100,50 800x600. Cause: await self.set_window_state(state='normal') uses the default left=0, top=0, width=1280, height=720.

Headless lines: 'set_window_size(200,100,900,700) after maximize: state=normal l=0 t=0 w=1280 h=720'; 'tab.maximize() ... plain restore: state=normal l=0 t=0 w=1280 h=720' versus 'raw maximize ... plain restore: state=normal l=100 t=50 w=800 h=600'; 'raw bounds w/o state while maximized: state=normal l=100 t=50 w=800 h=600'. The code comes from the bulk import 5c1a005. Its comment covers only the normal-to-non-normal direction, and no test exercises it.
groups.refinements: The 0,0 1280x720 result seen in A6.6 actually comes from A6.7's reset. The core of A6.6 (requested bounds dropped while the window is non-normal) holds on its own, as the raw-CDP control shows. Through zendriver's own API, A6.7 is visible only as the headful jump/resize before minimize, maximize or fullscreen, or when the window is restored by raw CDP or by the user, because medimize() always sends 0,0,1280,720 anyway. Headful maximize/minimize could not be checked because Xvfb has no window manager; fullscreen was checked headful. It needs a sequence where the size is set after a state change, which is unusual for most scripts.

groups.summary: All five members reproduce in real headless Chromium. Browser.setDownloadBehavior is sent with no browser_context_id, so it always targets the default context. zendriver tracks the result per Tab (_download_behavior). DownloadExpectation enables download events, but set_download_path sends events_enabled unset (false) on the same session. Results: (1) ex.value never resolves when download_file or set_download_path runs inside expect_download; (2) context tabs ignore set_download_path and expect_download times out; (3) one tab's download_file or expect_download silently redirects another tab's downloads. I found no keepalive or timeout that ends the ex.value wait. DownloadExpectation's future has no timeout.
